title: CPUNET nrfx_timer.c duplicate-singleton adoption (P4 iteration 28)

singleton_state.shipped_address_proof: R_ARM_ABS32 relocation into .bss.m_cb at +0x34 of the stock .text.nrfx_timer_disable section; the shipped image word at 0x01035028+0x34 minus the in-place addend resolves to 0x21004af8, and the same value is reached independently from .text.nrfx_timer_init (+0x68), .text.nrfx_timer_uninit (+0x38) and .text.nrfx_timer_2_irq_handler (+0x64).
singleton_state.reconstruction_pin: g_net_gpiote_evt_handler_table (a mis-name; the object is nrfx_timer's control block, not a GPIOTE handler table)

unit_completeness.note: Every nrfx_timer.c function that the shipped firmware contains is byte-identical to the stock section; the other 13 were --gc-sections'd out of the shipped link exactly as they are out of ours.  The unit is stock and UNMODIFIED.

method: Indexed every .text.* input section of every stock archive member this net link consumes (2506 sections, 40 archives), with a 4-byte mask at each relocation offset.

Compared the shipped netcore_image.bin bytes at each recovered function's analysis VA against every same-length section under that mask; a claim requires agreement over EVERY unmasked byte of the WHOLE section.
Independently re-scanned the whole image with a sliding window for each nrfx_timer.c section, to prove no function of the unit sits at a different VA and that the unit is not partially vendored.

measured_defects_this_displacement_fixes.detail: The recovered FUN_01034f24 (timer_configure) carries the base frequency literal 0x000f4240 = 1,000,000 Hz; the stock section and the shipped image both carry 0x00f42400 = 16,000,000 Hz.  With the ESB config frequency of 1,000,000 Hz the recovered body computes prescaler = ctz(1) = 0 and programs TIMER2 at 16 MHz, i.e. the ESB timer ran SIXTEEN TIMES too fast; the stock body computes ctz(16) = 4 and programs 1 MHz.  This is a transcription defect the parity harness could not see (the literal is inside the reconstructed body, so original and candidate agree with each other).

MEASURED on /private/tmp/g1-i28base-net (probe4/probe5, Renode watchpoint on the state byte): nrfx_timer_init DOES succeed and writes m_cb.state = 1 at 0x21001fb0 (pc 0x0102d0ac), and the byte is later zeroed by memcpy (pc 0x0103c514) called from FUN_0102b3f0+0x66 with dest 0x21001eff = g_net_ctrl_status_byte (shipped 0x21004c9f, block g1_net_ram_blk_21004c98 + 0x7).  In the SHIPPED address space that copy runs from 0x21004c9f upwards and cannot touch 0x21004b00; in the compressed relocation-block space the two objects are only 0xb1 bytes apart, so it does.  Moving m_cb out of the block space into the stock .bss removes the aliasing.

not_aliased.reason: timer_configure is a file-local symbol ('t') in the stock object, so a linker PROVIDE cannot name it.  Its only referrer in the recovered corpus is FUN_01034fa8, which is displaced in the same batch, so the exclusion leaves no undefined reference.
nrfx_timer_disable's only recovered referrer is FUN_01035068, displaced in the same batch.  A defensive PROVIDE is still emitted; PROVIDE only defines a symbol that is actually referenced.
